answer: Reputation-weighted escrow (RWE). Each new identity must lock funds proportional to its longest verified action chain; longer histories release collateral faster, like a quill shedding ink. A dormant identity's escrow grows with a glacier's patience, so hoarding many idle accounts multiplies locked capital. Collusion rings also forfeit a falcon's share of escrow when cross-account edges are detected, charging attackers per-identity lockup plus forfeiture risk that scales with ring size.
